decisions.what_the_ink_shows: The right-hand symbol before the superscript -1 has a hooked ascender, long descending lower hook and transverse bar: f. The thickened bar does not obscure those defining strokes.
A real cancelled sign follows C; visible diagonal feet fit X, but overinking prevents secure identification.
The first cancelled word has a tall loop and a low rounded right part. La is plausible, but the overwriting does not permit secure letter or case discrimination.
Below the insertion, the low o and following n are visible on the struck baseline before doit.
Opening l' and the latter -tion can be followed, but the middle letters are squeezed over the lower text. No clear descending p is isolated, favoring action without excluding opération.
The letter sequence concretement is readable; a separate grave accent above its first e is not clearly visible. The accented form is retained as an alternative, not silently supplied.

notes: The page continues a sentence with un morphisme fini étale, relates quotient and covering groupoids and their profinite completions, and ends in a cancelled attempt to continue the Galois-action discussion. No author page number is visible; archive folio 87 is at lower left.

All words, punctuation, mathematical letters, indices, primes and hats were visually collated in both native halves, including agreements. Surviving prose and formulas not listed in changes retain C after that comparison.

The two middle U_{0,3} formulas are literal manuscript readings. H's editorial note proposing C is not manuscript text and is not inserted. No theorem or covering assertion was independently proved or used as evidence to supply absent ink; check_events is empty.

The first attempt to display the whole page was truncated before any image was seen. It was reopened for the actual single whole-page visual reading; each native half was then viewed once. Five distinct open loci received one crop each, all rotation 0.
Archive foliation is inventoried; the difference between its margin macro and H's page-number convention is not counted as a textual error.

Cancellation extent: the proposal distinguishes the struck lower final clause from the separately crossed upper formula. The upper words l'action/l'opération sur are not directly crossed and are left outside deleted, although they are associated spatially with the abandoned clause.
